{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio Hosting and License Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio)
**Re:** Playbook review findings and negotiation positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. Of the 18 rules assessed, **6 are compliant and require no redline**, and **12 require change** — including **four critical items** (indemnification, IP/Customer Data ownership, limitation of liability, and — at high severity — the absence of any customer exit right).

The commercial architecture is, in several respects, favourable to us: the hosting licence in Section 2.1 is perpetual and irrevocable, sublicensing to our Customers is expressly permitted, Section 2.4 gives us protection against Commerce One approaching Corio Customers, and there are no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment, non-solicit or customer-payable liquidated damages provisions.

The risk is concentrated in the exit and allocation-of-risk provisions. Three points drive our position:

- **Liability cap is illusory.** Section 9 caps recovery at amounts *actually paid* by Corio and only for the *specific transaction* to which the liability relates — so early in the term, or under Exhibit B revenue-share fees, there is effectively no recovery. Carve-outs cover only the Section 8 IP indemnity, with nothing for confidentiality, data or security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud.
- **Our own work product can transfer to the Vendor.** Section 13.5 gives us ownership of Developments but flips title to Commerce One wherever Commerce One supports those Developments on an ongoing basis. That is an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor and is a walk-away position. There is also no statement anywhere that we and our Customers retain rights in data hosted on the Corio Servers or passing through MarketSite.net.
- **We are locked in with no exit and no transition.** A five-year initial term with automatic renewals, no termination for convenience, no cap on renewal pricing (Exhibit B simply says "Year 2–5, and beyond: [*]"), and no transition-assistance or data-return obligation on expiry. The only "return or destroy" language sits in Section 11.3 and, as drafted, could support unilateral destruction of our data.

Secondary items — indemnity scope, licence scope for Affiliates and contractors, audit mechanics, arbitration, warranty duration and insurance — are all addressable with short, targeted edits.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8 INDEMNIFICATION. | § 8.1 IP indemnity with procedure and procure/modify/refund remedies is acceptable and § 9 carves § 8 out of the cap. Missing limbs for breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to or disclosure of our and our Customers' data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct. New § 8.3 adds them using the § 8.1 procedure and confirms the § 8.2 IP-specific exclusions do not apply. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES. | § 13.5 carve-out transfers ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One whenever it supports them on an ongoing basis — an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor (walk-away). Support should be handled by licence, not title. No Customer Data ownership statement anywhere (§ 10 only cross-refers to an NDA). Remove the carve-out; confirm Corio/Customer retain all rights in Customer Data with no assignment or joint ownership. Commerce One's § 2.8 ownership of the Software is untouched and acceptable. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. | Cap limited to amounts "actually paid" and only for "the transaction which the liability relates to" — not aggregate, no 12-month basis, no USD 1,000,000 floor, illusory early in term. Only § 8 is carved out; nothing for confidentiality (§ 10), data/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement, and Corio's fee obligations are not carved out. Reset to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000, aggregate, plus a single Excluded Claims sentence. Mutual consequential-damages exclusion left untouched. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | § 14.1 is mutual but has no affiliate carve-out for Corio, no reasonableness standard on consent, and a competitor carve-back that applies to both parties — letting Commerce One block our merger, acquisition or asset sale. Add the affiliate right, a "not unreasonably withheld or delayed" standard, and confine the competitor restriction to Commerce One's assignments. § 11 has no change-of-control trigger, so only the mechanics need fixing. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Compliant** | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Corio. All § 2 grants and the § 12 escrow licence are expressly nonexclusive; § 2.7 restrictions are ordinary IP scope limits. No requirements, minimum-purchase, preferred-provider or non-procurement language. Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding; § 13.6 preserves independent development. § 2.4 exclusivity runs in our favour and is preserved. No redline. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Compliant** | § 4 FEES. | No liquidated damages, penalty, late-payment interest, minimum fee, early-termination fee or acceleration payable by Corio across §§ 4, 9, 11 and Exhibit B. § 11.2 termination simply ends the Agreement; § 11.1 non-renewal carries no fee. The Exhibit B revenue share is usage-based consideration, not a penalty. Refunds under §§ 3 and 7 run in our favour. No redline. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. | Grant is otherwise favourable (perpetual and irrevocable hosting licence in § 2.1; perpetual, fully paid-up internal-use licence in § 2.2; sublicensing to Customers permitted; nontransferability carve-out to § 14.1 covers successors). Gap: no rights run to Corio's Affiliates or to contractors acting on our behalf ("Affiliate" appears nowhere), and § 2.2 is confined to "Corio's internal business operations". Add new § 2.11 extending the § 2 licences to Affiliates and contractors, with Corio responsible for their compliance. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Compliant** | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. | No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restraint on Corio. § 2.7 protects Commerce One's Software only; §§ 2.4 and 14.8 protect our resale and subcontracting freedom; § 13.6 preserves independent development. "Territory" and "Corio Market Segment" limit only the licence scope (and § 2.10 obliges Commerce One not unreasonably to withhold worldwide expansion). Exhibit D is non-binding. No redline. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | Five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals; § 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. No customer convenience right anywhere (other exits limited to acceptance-test failure under § 3 and warranty/IP remedies under §§ 7–8). Commerce One likewise has no convenience right, which matches our position. Add new § 11.4 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with refund of prepaid fees and confirming no Commerce One convenience exit. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 4 FEES. | § 4.4 already delivers once-yearly frequency, an independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, Commerce One cost-bearing unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no system access. Deviates by leaving notice and timing merely "reasonable" and not binding the auditor to confidentiality (§ 10 binds only the parties). Add 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, and an auditor confidentiality undertaking; confirm no system access. Frequency and cost allocation undisturbed. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | California law is within the accepted list and appropriate (both parties California-based). Deviation is mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration instead of courts. Seat is domestic (San Francisco), so not a walk-away. We take the fallback — California law and courts — swapping arbitration for exclusive jurisdiction of the San Francisco state and federal courts and conforming the heading. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Compliant** | PRICING | No MFN, best-pricing or price-parity obligation in either direction; searches for parity language returned nothing. Exhibit B pricing, revenue-sharing fees, payment terms and § 4 are fixed fees and revenue shares with no parity or price-matching undertaking by Corio. §§ 2.4 and 2.9 leave future product licensing to terms "as the parties may agree". Caveat: certain Exhibit B and § 2.4 figures are redacted ("[*]") — re-run this rule against unredacted text. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Compliant** | PRICING | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay or shortfall penalty on Corio. Exhibit B prices licences, MarketSite.net access and maintenance as fees for services actually ordered; user volume is "Unlimited"; revenue share is a percentage of revenue actually invoiced; implementation is time-and-materials with a cap. The 40-Authorized-User floor only conditions the revenue-share exemption for the initial 3,000 licences, and § 4.4 provides true-up/refund rather than penalty — consistent with the playbook. Exhibit D is non-binding. Five-year term addressed under the term/exit rules. No redline. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Compliant** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant on Corio; searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce" returned no hits. "Employ" appears only in § 13.5 (Commerce One personnel NDAs), § 14.5 (independent-contractor disclaimer) and Exhibit D ¶ 5 (each party assigns a sales/marketing employee). §§ 13 and 14 read in full contain no hiring restraint despite the secondment of Commerce One personnel under §§ 13.1–13.3. No redline. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | § 11.1 meets the preferred structure on renewal length (one year) and exit (30 days' notice, exercisable by Corio), but omits a 60-day vendor renewal reminder and any cap on renewal pricing — Exhibit B states only "Year 2–5, and beyond: [*]" and § 4 contains no uplift limit. Add the 60-day reminder and cap renewal increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 5% fallback offered. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | No transition-assistance or data-return obligation. § 11.3 preserves customer-access rights and surviving support, and § 12 provides source-code escrow, but nothing requires migration assistance on exit or return of our and our Customers' data (including data held through MarketSite.net) in machine-readable form, or deletion with certification. The generic § 11.3 "return or destroy" line is not an export right and could support unilateral destruction of our data. Insert new § 11.4: up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable data return, and deletion with written certification (subject to retention needed for surviving support obligations and law). |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER. | § 7.3 conformance warranty runs only 60 days from the **Effective Date** (not delivery or acceptance) and is hard-capped at 31 December 1999 — below even the playbook fallback, and capable of expiring before or immediately after deployment. Malicious-code warranty is limited to the same window and to code "willfully introduced". No professional-and-workmanlike warranty for the § 5 installation, implementation, support, training and professional services. The § 7.3 remedy (correction, replacement, refund of prepaid fees on termination) is acceptable, and the disclaimer addresses implied warranties only. Redline limited to duration (12 months from delivery, sunset removed), continuous malicious-code coverage, and a services warranty with re-performance/refund. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | No insurance clause (the sole use of "insurance" is in the Net Revenue definition), yet Commerce One operations, consulting and engineering personnel — and third-party integrators it may assign — work alongside Corio personnel on the hosted environment and may access Corio and Customer data. Insert new § 14.10 requiring CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M where our data is processed, workers' compensation, and certificates on request; renumber Complete Understanding. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Vendor ownership of our work product (§ 13.5).** The carve-out transferring title in Corio-created Developments to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis is an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor — expressly our walk-away position. Ongoing support must be handled by licence, not by title transfer. This must come out.

2. **Customer Data rights.** Coupled with item 1, the Agreement nowhere confirms that we and our Customers retain rights in data hosted on the Corio Servers or passing through MarketSite.net (§ 10 only cross-refers to an NDA), while § 11.3 could be read to permit unilateral destruction of that data on exit. We need an express retention-of-rights statement plus the § 11.4 return-and-certified-deletion mechanic.

3. **A cap that delivers no recovery (§ 9).** "Amounts actually paid" for "the transaction which the liability relates to" is not a meaningful cap early in a five-year term or against Exhibit B revenue-share fees, and confidentiality, data/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud all sit inside it. We need the aggregate greater-of-12-months'-fees-or-US$1,000,000 basis and the Excluded Claims sentence.

*Note:* the governing-law point is **not** a walk-away. The arbitration forum deviates from our position, but California law is acceptable and the seat is domestic, so we take the fallback of California law and courts rather than pushing New York.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the twelve deviation/missing items, marked with the `[Playbook]` comment prefix. The six compliant rules (exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitments, non-solicitation) require no edit and should be recorded as cleared.
2. **Lead the negotiation on the three walk-away items** — § 13.5 ownership carve-out, Customer Data rights, and the § 9 cap and carve-outs. These should be settled before we trade on the medium and low items.
3. **Bundle the exit package** as a single ask: the new § 11.4 (30-day convenience right with refund of prepaid fees, plus six months' transition assistance and certified data deletion) together with the § 11.1 renewal reminder and the renewal uplift cap. Offer the 5% uplift fallback if 3%/CPI is resisted.
4. **Obtain the unredacted Exhibit B and § 2.4 pricing** and re-run the MFN rule against it; the compliant finding is expressly qualified pending sight of the redacted figures. Confirm at the same time what "Year 2–5, and beyond: [*]" contains, given the absence of any uplift cap in § 4.
5. **Package the lower-friction items** — the § 8.3 indemnity limbs, the § 2.11 Affiliate and contractor licence extension, the § 4.4 audit mechanics, the § 7.3 warranty duration and services warranty, the governing-law forum swap, and the new § 14.10 insurance covenant — as a single administrative clean-up tranche.
6. **Confirm insurance capacity with Commerce One** before finalising § 14.10 limits, and request certificates of insurance for the seconded operations, consulting and engineering personnel and any third-party integrators contemplated by §§ 13.1–13.3.

*The findings above were compiled without independent verification of the underlying extracts; section references and characterisations are taken as supplied.*"}
